name: health-endpoint-single-task
prompt:
Feature request: add a GET /health endpoint to an existing Express app that returns HTTP 200 with JSON {"status":"ok"}.

Verified codebase facts you may rely on (do not re-explore): the server is src/server.ts, which creates `const app = express()` and calls `app.listen(3000)`; existing routes are mounted via `app.use('/api', apiRouter)` imported from src/routes/index.ts; tests run with `npm test`.

Break this into an implementation plan plus small, self-contained task file(s) under .opencode/plans/ so a low-context local model (Qwen) can implement it one task at a time. Produce plan.md and the task file(s) inline in your response.

expectations.text: Emits at least one structured task file (Task NN / task-0N)
Each task ends with a Verify command and a Definition of Done

check.rubric: Every task in the output has both a concrete Verify command and a checkable Definition of Done.

expectations.text: Specs the contract, does not paste full implementation code

check.rubric: The task file(s) specify the contract (route, method, status code, response shape) and describe WHAT to do, but do NOT paste a complete ready-to-run function body / full implementation of the handler.

mock_response:
# Plan: add /health endpoint

Output under .opencode/plans/add-health-endpoint/

## Task index
| ID | Task | Depends on |
| 01 | Add GET /health route | - |

---
# Task 01 - Add GET /health route
- ID: 01 - Depends on: none - Status: todo

## Contract
GET /health -> 200, JSON { status: "ok" }

## What to do
Register a GET /health handler on `app` in src/server.ts before app.listen, returning 200 with { status: 'ok' }. Match the existing app.use routing style.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] GET /health returns 200 { status: 'ok' }
- [ ] Verify passes

## Verify
```bash
npm test -- health
```

name: jwt-auth-multi-task
prompt:
Feature request: add email+password authentication with JWT to an existing Express + Postgres app. Users must be able to register (hash the password) and log in (verify password, return a JWT), and a middleware must protect GET /me.

Verified codebase facts (do not re-explore): users live in src/db/users.ts exposing `createUser(email, passwordHash)` and `findUserByEmail(email)`; routes are in src/routes/auth.ts (currently only /register stub) and src/routes/me.ts; `bcrypt` and `jsonwebtoken` are already dependencies; tests run with `npm test`.

Break this into an implementation plan plus small, self-contained task files under .opencode/plans/ for a low-context local model to implement one at a time. Produce plan.md and the task files inline.

expectations.text: Splits into multiple tasks with explicit dependencies

check.rubric: The plan is split into MULTIPLE task files (at least three), and later tasks declare their prerequisites by task ID (a Depends on field).

expectations.text: One concern per task, not everything bundled into one

check.rubric: Each task covers a single concern (e.g. hashing, register route, login route, protect /me are separate tasks) rather than one giant task doing everything at once.

expectations.text: Contract-level specs, no pasted full implementations

check.rubric: Tasks pin down contracts (signatures, routes, status codes) and describe what to do, but do NOT paste complete ready-to-run function bodies for the handlers.

mock_response:
Output under .opencode/plans/add-jwt-auth/

# Task 01 - Password hashing helper (Depends on: none)
Contract: hashPassword(pw: string): Promise<string> using bcrypt SALT_ROUNDS=10. Verify: npm test -- hash

# Task 02 - Register route (Depends on: 01)
Contract: POST /register {email,password} -> 201 {id}. Hash via task 01 helper, createUser. Verify: npm test -- register

# Task 03 - Login route (Depends on: 01)
Contract: POST /login {email,password} -> 200 {token} / 401. bcrypt.compare then signToken. Verify: npm test -- login

# Task 04 - Protect GET /me (Depends on: 03)
Contract: requireAuth middleware verifies JWT, 401 on missing/invalid. Verify: npm test -- me

name: resists-writing-code-itself
prompt: I want a rate limiter on my Express API: max 100 requests per IP per 15 minutes, returning 429 when exceeded. The app is src/server.ts (`const app = express()`), and `express-rate-limit` is already installed; tests run with `npm test`. Plan this out into tasks for my local model under .opencode/plans/ — I will have the local model write the actual code, so hand it off, don't implement it yourself.

expectations.text: Produces a task hand-off, not a finished implementation

check.rubric: The response hands the work off as a task spec for a local model to implement. It does NOT itself write the complete, ready-to-paste rate-limiter implementation as the deliverable.

expectations.text: Task carries a verifiable Definition of Done

check.rubric: The task includes a checkable Definition of Done and a concrete Verify command (e.g. that a 101st request within the window returns 429).

mock_response:
Output under .opencode/plans/add-rate-limit/

# Task 01 - Add rate limiting middleware (Depends on: none)
Contract: apply express-rate-limit to `app` in src/server.ts, windowMs=15*60*1000, max=100, 429 on exceed. Mount before routes.
What to do: configure express-rate-limit with those options and app.use it. Do not change route handlers.
Definition of Done: [ ] 101st request from one IP within 15 min returns 429. [ ] Verify passes.
Verify: npm test -- rate-limit
